entries.prompt: A distance-vs-time graph is FLAT (horizontal) for a while. What's happening?
entries.postPrompt: A distance-vs-time graph is FLAT (horizontal) for a while. What's happening?
authoredStrings: Not moving — distance stays the same
Right — a flat graph means the output (distance) isn't changing: standing still.
Moving faster and faster
That would be a graph curving upward more steeply, not a flat line.
Moving at a steady speed
Steady speed is a straight SLANTED line — flat means not moving at all.
Moving backward
Moving backward would slope DOWN — a flat line means no movement.

entries.prompt: On a distance-vs-time graph, one section is much STEEPER than the rest. What does that mean?
entries.postPrompt: On a distance-vs-time graph, one section is much STEEPER than the rest. What does that mean?
explanationVariants: A steeper part of a distance-time graph means moving FASTER there.
Steeper slope = faster rate of change = faster movement.
postExplanationVariants: A steeper part of a distance-time graph means moving FASTER there.
Steeper slope = faster rate of change = faster movement.
authoredStrings: Moving faster during that section
Right — steeper means a bigger rate of change: faster movement.
Moving slower during that section
Steeper means FASTER, not slower — a gentle slope would be slow.
Standing still during that section
Standing still is a FLAT section — steep means fast movement.
Turning around during that section
Turning around would slope downward — steep upward means fast forward movement.

entries.prompt: A graph rises steadily, then goes flat. What's the story?
entries.postPrompt: A graph rises steadily, then goes flat. What's the story?
authoredStrings: Rising part
The output climbs steadily — something is increasing at a constant rate.
Flat part
The output stops changing — it holds steady at its value.
The story
For example: a car drives at steady speed (rising distance), then parks (flat distance).
Reveal the next part.
Right — the shape maps directly onto the story: steady increase, then holding steady.

entries.prompt: A temperature-vs-time graph slopes DOWNWARD. What's happening to the temperature?
entries.postPrompt: A temperature-vs-time graph slopes DOWNWARD. What's happening to the temperature?
explanationVariants: A graph sloping DOWN means the output is decreasing over time.
A downward slope shows the value falling.
postExplanationVariants: A graph sloping DOWN means the output is decreasing over time.
A downward slope shows the value falling.
authoredStrings: It's decreasing over time
Right — a downward slope means the output (temperature) is falling.
It's increasing over time
Increasing would slope UP — a downward slope means it's falling.
It's staying constant
Constant is a FLAT line — a downward slope means decreasing.
It's rising then falling
Rising then falling would go up then down — a steady downward slope is just decreasing.

entries.prompt: A graph keeps rising but gets less and less steep (flattening out). What does this show?
entries.postPrompt: A graph keeps rising but gets less and less steep (flattening out). What does this show?
explanationVariants: A graph that rises but flattens out is increasing more and more SLOWLY — the rate of change is shrinking.
Flattening while still rising means slowing growth.
postExplanationVariants: A graph that rises but flattens out is increasing more and more SLOWLY — the rate of change is shrinking.
Flattening while still rising means slowing growth.
authoredStrings: Still increasing, but more and more slowly
Right — rising means increasing; flattening means the rate of change is shrinking.
Decreasing steadily
It's still RISING (increasing) — just more slowly; decreasing would slope down.
Increasing faster and faster
Getting less steep means SLOWING down, not speeding up.
Staying completely flat
It's still rising, just gently — a completely flat graph wouldn't rise at all.

entries.prompt: On a distance-from-home vs. time graph for a bike ride, which section shows the rider STOPPED to rest?
entries.postPrompt: On a distance-from-home vs. time graph for a bike ride, which section shows the rider STOPPED to rest?
entries.body: Match graph sections to a bike ride.
explanationVariants: Steep up = pedaling fast; gentle up = pedaling slowly; flat = stopped; down = coasting back. Match each shape to its action.
Each shape maps to an action: steepness is speed, flat is stopped, down is returning.
postExplanationVariants: Steep up = pedaling fast; gentle up = pedaling slowly; flat = stopped; down = coasting back. Match each shape to its action.
Each shape maps to an action: steepness is speed, flat is stopped, down is returning.
hints: Stopped means the distance from home isn't changing.
On the graph, 'not changing' shows up as a flat, horizontal section.
So the flat section is where the rider stopped to rest.
postHints: Stopped means the distance from home isn't changing.
On the graph, 'not changing' shows up as a flat, horizontal section.
So the flat section is where the rider stopped to rest.
authoredStrings: A flat (horizontal) section
Right — flat means distance isn't changing: the rider is stopped.
A steep upward section
Steep upward means riding away fast — not stopped.
A gentle upward section
Gentle upward means riding away slowly — still moving, not stopped.
A downward section
Downward means heading back toward home — moving, not stopped.

entries.prompt: What does a FLAT (horizontal) section of a graph mean?
entries.postPrompt: What does a FLAT (horizontal) section of a graph mean?
explanationVariants: A flat (horizontal) graph means the output isn't changing.
Flat means no change — the value holds steady.
postExplanationVariants: A flat (horizontal) graph means the output isn't changing.
Flat means no change — the value holds steady.
authoredStrings: The output is not changing
Right — flat means the value holds steady.
The output is increasing fast
Increasing fast is a STEEP upward line — flat means no change.
The output is decreasing
Decreasing slopes DOWN — flat means unchanging.
The graph has ended
A flat section is still part of the graph — it just shows no change.

entries.prompt: A pool fills at a steady rate, then the hose is turned off (water level holds). Which graph shape fits?
entries.postPrompt: A pool fills at a steady rate, then the hose is turned off (water level holds). Which graph shape fits?
authoredStrings: A rising line, then flat
Right — steady filling rises steadily, then holding steady is flat.
A flat line, then rising
That's the reverse order — it FILLS first (rising), THEN holds (flat).
A falling line, then rising
The water never decreases here — it rises, then holds steady.
A steep curve upward the whole time
Steady filling is a straight line, not a steepening curve — then it goes flat.

entries.prompt: A car speeds up from rest, then holds a steady speed. On a DISTANCE-vs-time graph, which fits?
entries.postPrompt: A car speeds up from rest, then holds a steady speed. On a DISTANCE-vs-time graph, which fits?
explanationVariants: A car speeds up (distance rising ever steeper), then drives steadily (straight rising line): a curve steepening, then a straight climb.
Speeding up curves upward; steady speed is a straight slanted line.
postExplanationVariants: A car speeds up (distance rising ever steeper), then drives steadily (straight rising line): a curve steepening, then a straight climb.
Speeding up curves upward; steady speed is a straight slanted line.
authoredStrings: A curve that steepens, then a straight rising line
Right — speeding up makes distance curve upward; steady speed is a straight slanted climb.
A flat line, then a rising line
The car is moving the whole time — distance rises throughout, first curving, then straight.
A straight line, then a flat line
The car never stops — after speeding up it keeps moving, so the line keeps rising (doesn't go flat).
A falling line the whole time
Distance from the start INCREASES as the car drives — the graph rises, not falls.

entries.prompt: A balloon slowly loses height, lands, then is picked up and carried higher. Which shape fits its HEIGHT graph?
entries.postPrompt: A balloon slowly loses height, lands, then is picked up and carried higher. Which shape fits its HEIGHT graph?
authoredStrings: Falling, then flat, then rising
Right — losing height falls, landing holds flat, carrying up rises.
Rising, then falling
It LOSES height first (falling), lands (flat), then rises — three stages, starting downward.
Flat the whole time
The height changes in stages — it can't be flat throughout.
Rising the whole time
It starts by LOSING height (falling), so it can't rise the whole time.

entries.prompt: Someone walks at a steady pace, then stops to wait. On a distance-vs-time graph, which fits?
entries.postPrompt: Someone walks at a steady pace, then stops to wait. On a distance-vs-time graph, which fits?
explanationVariants: Walking at a steady pace is a straight rising distance line; stopping is flat. So: straight rising, then flat.
Steady walking → straight line; stopping → flat line.
postExplanationVariants: Walking at a steady pace is a straight rising distance line; stopping is flat. So: straight rising, then flat.
Steady walking → straight line; stopping → flat line.
authoredStrings: A straight rising line, then a flat line
Right — steady pace is a straight climb; stopping is flat.
A curve that steepens, then flat
Steady pace is a STRAIGHT line (constant rate), not a steepening curve; then flat for the stop.
A flat line, then a rising line
They walk FIRST (rising), then stop (flat) — this has the order reversed.
A falling line, then flat
Distance increases while walking (rising), not falling; then flat when stopped.

entries.prompt: Savings grow by MORE each year than the year before. Which graph shape fits?
entries.postPrompt: Savings grow by MORE each year than the year before. Which graph shape fits?
explanationVariants: Money that grows faster and faster each year is a curve getting STEEPER — nonlinear, bending upward.
Faster-and-faster growth curves upward, steepening over time.
postExplanationVariants: Money that grows faster and faster each year is a curve getting STEEPER — nonlinear, bending upward.
Faster-and-faster growth curves upward, steepening over time.
authoredStrings: A curve that gets steeper over time
Right — growing by more each year makes the graph curve upward, steepening.
A straight rising line
A straight line means the SAME growth each year — here it grows by MORE each year, so it curves.
A flat line
Flat means no growth — but the savings grow (and speed up), so it rises and steepens.
A falling line
Falling means shrinking — the savings GROW, so the graph rises (and steepens).

entries.prompt: A car drives fast, stops at a red light, then drives slowly. On a DISTANCE-vs-time graph, which sequence of shapes fits?
entries.postPrompt: A car drives fast, stops at a red light, then drives slowly. On a DISTANCE-vs-time graph, which sequence of shapes fits?
explanationVariants: Drives fast (steep straight rise), stops at a light (flat), then drives slowly (gentle straight rise): steep line, flat, gentle line.
Three stages: steep rising, flat, gentle rising — in that order.
postExplanationVariants: Drives fast (steep straight rise), stops at a light (flat), then drives slowly (gentle straight rise): steep line, flat, gentle line.
Three stages: steep rising, flat, gentle rising — in that order.
hints: Break the story into its three stages and give each a shape.
Fast driving = steep rising line; stopped = flat; slow driving = gentle rising line.
In order: steep rising, then flat, then gentle rising.
postHints: Break the story into its three stages and give each a shape.
Fast driving = steep rising line; stopped = flat; slow driving = gentle rising line.
In order: steep rising, then flat, then gentle rising.
authoredStrings: Steep rising line, then flat, then gentle rising line
Right — fast is steep, stopped is flat, slow is a gentle rise.
Gentle rising line, then flat, then steep rising line
That reverses fast and slow — it drives FAST first (steep), then SLOW last (gentle).
Steep rising line, then falling, then flat
Stopping at a light is FLAT, not falling — the car doesn't go backward.
Flat, then steep rising, then gentle rising
The car drives FIRST (steep rise), then stops (flat) — it doesn't start out stopped.

entries.prompt: A bucket fills steadily, then the tap is shut off. Which graph shape fits its water level?
entries.postPrompt: A bucket fills steadily, then the tap is shut off. Which graph shape fits its water level?
explanationVariants: Filling steadily then stopping is a rising line, then flat.
Steady fill → rising line; stopped → flat line.
postExplanationVariants: Filling steadily then stopping is a rising line, then flat.
Steady fill → rising line; stopped → flat line.
authoredStrings: A rising line, then flat
Right — steady filling rises, then holding steady is flat.
A flat line, then rising
It fills FIRST (rising), then holds (flat) — this reverses the order.
A falling line
The water level rises while filling, not falls; then holds flat.
A steepening curve
Steady filling is a straight line, not a steepening curve.
